headline: Bank of America is no longer in talks to help run the planned Hong Kong share listing of the Chinese AI company Moonshot AI, Bloomberg reports, as Moonshot faces scrutiny in the US.
score_reason: Pool score kept: one bank dropping out of a listing roster, with no detail on the US scrutiny and no sign the listing is cancelled.
importance_line: Investors following Moonshot's planned Hong Kong listing lose one named large bank from a roster that is still forming, and Bloomberg ties it to US scrutiny of the company, but what the scrutiny involves is not stated, no mandate was ever signed, and the listing itself is not reported cancelled.
summary: Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter, that Bank of America is no longer part of the potential group of banks working on the initial public offering of Moonshot AI, the Beijing maker of the Kimi chatbot, because talks about an overall-coordinator role in Hong Kong never led to a formal mandate (a signed appointment). New today is the bank's exit: our 12 Oct 2026 edition carried a Reuters exclusive that Moonshot's executives were in talks to settle a shareholder's legal claim before the listing, and Bloomberg adds that the Chinese company faces scrutiny in the US.
notes: Bloomberg is paywalled after two paragraphs; the TradingView/Seeking Alpha summary was also read. Follow-up of the 12 Oct 2026 edition (Moonshot shareholder dispute, Reuters exclusive).
